- temporary surge credits to smooth the Q4-to-Q1 transition
- a short-term uplift to our commit (1–2 quarters) with a price hold so we can avoid higher overage rates

I attached our internal usage dump for the quarter so you can see the shape. Procurement is looped for the contract implications.

We'd like to align on an approach this week if possible — do you have 30 minutes tomorrow?

Thanks,
Jordan Ellis

Jordan — thanks for the visibility and for sending the usage export. I pulled a quick pass with CS (Monica) and we have a couple of pragmatic paths you can choose from depending on how Procurement wants to structure the amendment:

Option A — Surge stabilization credits (fastest)
- Redwood issues one-off surge credits equal to 25% of the overage for Q4 (applied against December invoice)
- We pair this with a short-term commit uplift for Q1 to keep your latency SLOs intact
- Pros: immediate relief, minimal paperwork

Option B — Quarter-limited commit + price hold (clean contract path)
- Move you up one commit tier for 90 days; keep current committed pricing for that window
- If you hit the uplifted commit, the uplift stays; otherwise it reverts at quarter end
- Pros: predictable unit cost for the spike period, aligns with procurement processes

Option C — Hybrid: smaller immediate credit + discounted temporary committed add-on

If you can confirm Procurement's tolerance for a 90-day amendment, I can draft a short-form amendment and run it through Marcus for approval. If you prefer credits, we can issue them quickly and draft a follow-up commit amendment.

I'm free 10:30–12:00 PT tomorrow for a 30m sync. Suggested agenda: confirm preferred path, landing commit amounts, and DocuSign timeline.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Cell: (415) 555-0137

PS — attaching a one-page template amendment in the follow-up (draft will be non-binding until legal signs).

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — unexpected Q4 surge and stabilization request (internal)

Internal — we should thread a clean offer that balances revenue protection and the customer's need for predictability. My quick proposal for negotiation bullets: 

- Short-term price hold: keep existing committed $/k token rate for a 90-day uplift up to 2x current commit. If they exceed 2x, overage rates apply at current published levels.
- Surge credit: one-time credit equal to 20% of the incremental spend above current commit for Q4 (applied as invoice credit).
- Commitment incentive: if they convert the uplift into a multi-quarter commit within 60 days, apply a 10% retroactive credit on the uplifted committed portion for the quarter.
- Contract mechanics: short amendment + optional 12-month addendum if they want a longer lock.

Why these numbers? 20% credit gives visible relief without muddying ARR too much; 2x uplift is large enough to cover the observed spike but capped to avoid open-ended exposure. The retroactive credit is a conversion incentive.

Action items: Aisha — draft amendment language for Option B/C that includes the 90-day price hold and the surge credit clause. Marcus — can you confirm if Finance can accept a retro credit flow? Monica — prep a quick MAP (mutual action plan) with key dates to share with Procurement.

-ben

Jordan / Procurement — thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation, here is the short-form summary of the path we discussed (we can turn this into a one-page amendment and send for legal review once you confirm):

1) 90-day stabilization uplift and price hold
- Effective 2026-12-01 for 90 days: CatalystCloud will be moved up one commit tier (estimated uplift to 2x baseline commit) with existing committed unit pricing held in place for the uplifted portion.

2) Q4 surge invoice credit
- Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to 20% of the incremental spend above CatalystCloud's baseline commit for November–December 2026 (applies as credit on the December invoice).

3) Conversion incentive
- If CatalystCloud converts the uplift into a new multi-quarter committed agreement within 60 days, Redwood will apply a retroactive 10% credit to the uplifted committed volume for the 90-day period.

4) Next steps & timeline
- I've attached draft_amendment_v2.docx with the legal-friendly language.
- Procurement: please confirm acceptance by 2026-12-04 so we can route to Legal and Finance.
- Target DocuSign issuance: 2026-12-06 (if accepted)
